queue.brief: Most project teams track issues in monday.com but never turn that log into a formal document — which means clients don't see it, it doesn't get signed off, and unresolved issues quietly become disputes. This post shows how to convert an existing issue log board into a professional issue register that clients can actually review and approve.

queue.title: How to Auto-Generate a Client-Facing Budget Reconciliation Report from Your monday.com Board at Project Close
queue.brief: When a project ends, clients want to know where every pound or dollar went — but pulling that into a formatted document from monday.com takes hours nobody has. This post shows how to turn your budget columns into a clean reconciliation report before the final invoice goes out.
queue.description: Target keyword: "budget reconciliation report monday.com". H2 sections: Why budget reconciliation gets skipped at project close / What monday.com columns you need to make this work (planned vs actual cost, task status, notes) / How to structure the reconciliation report clients actually expect / The manual process most teams use and where it breaks down / How to generate the document directly from your board data / What to include beyond the numbers (variance explanations, sign-off fields) / A real-world example of an agency reconciling a 12-week web project with 6 cost line items across 3 workstreams. queue.brief: A letter of engagement protects both sides before a contract is signed — but most teams skip it because writing one from scratch takes too long. This post shows how to pull the right data from your monday.com board and turn it into a professional engagement letter in minutes.

queue.brief: When a project is running late, the worst thing you can do is communicate it badly — but drafting a formal delay notification from scratch while the team is already under pressure is a recipe for vague, uncommitted language. This post shows how to pull the right data from monday.com and turn it into a professional delay notice clients can actually act on.
